incomplete_reason: [write-path-integrity] important admin/ui.ts — The `loadSubscribers` function sends `product_id` as a string from the dashboard table row, but the route handler expects it to be validated as numeric. However, the UI does not validate `product_external_id` before sending it; it reads directly from the response item: `bridge.call("/admin/subscribers", req)` passes `productId` which comes from `item.product_external_id` — a field from the database response. This is real data, so no issue here on second inspection. FIX: No change needed — product_external_id originates from the database (real data).

[write-path-integrity] important widget/widget.ts:109 — `itemDisplayName` is set to `titleEl.textContent?.trim() ?? ""` — when no title element is found, it falls back to an empty string. This empty string is then sent to the backend in `signupBody["item_display_name"] = safeDisplayName`, and on line 109 set to `safeDisplayName = itemDisplayName || "This item"`. The route handler accepts this, but the database persists `item_display_name` which is a TEXT reference field. The fallback `"This item"` is a hardcoded placeholder, not real user input or page data. FIX: Replace the fallback `"This item"` with a rejection or error state: do not submit the signup form if `itemDisplayName` cannot be read from the page.

[write-path-integrity] critical src/routes/webhook-handlers.ts:197 — In `handleOrdersPaid`, line 192: `const variantIdSet = new Set(variantIdStrings);` creates a set of variant IDs from the order line items. However, on line 197, for product-level entries, the match logic is `entry.variant_external_id !== null ? variantIdSet.has(...) : true;` — this means product-level waitlist entries are matched to ANY purchased variant without checking if that variant belongs to the product the shopper signed up for. A shopper could sign up for product A and be marked as converted when they buy a completely different product B if both have variants. FIX: For product-level entries, add an additional check to verify that the order contains at least one variant belonging to the matched product_external_id.

[shopify-effect-integrity] critical src/routes/cron.ts:96 — Line 96: `const variantGidToCheck = storedVariantGid ?? \`gid://shopify/ProductVariant/${variantIdStr}\`;` — the code fabricates a GID literal string as a fallback when `storedVariantGid` is NULL, instead of using only the canonical GID from the prior Shopify API response. FIX: Remove the fallback GID construction and skip the batch with an error log if storedVariantGid is not available, ensuring only Shopify-provided GIDs are used in API calls.

[persistence-safety] critical src/routes/webhook-handlers.ts:541 — The orders/paid handler performs an idempotency check using SELECT before INSERT: `const [existing] = await sql...SELECT id FROM conversions WHERE order_external_id...` followed by an early return if the row exists. This is a race condition: two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same order can both pass the SELECT check before either INSERT executes, creating duplicate conversion rows. The ON CONFLICT clause later is bypassed by the early return. FIX: Remove the SELECT idempotency check and rely solely on the ON CONFLICT (order_external_id, waitlist_entry_id) DO NOTHING clause to prevent duplicate conversions.
